summary: Tenant lease jitter causes pinned model demotion during canary wave
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary wave for gptx-alpha-3.1 we observed a subset of tenant sessions that were explicitly pinned to 3.1 being demoted to a degraded variant (3.0-quant) without an explicit rollback or pin change. Impact: Affected tenant (AtlasSearch) saw inconsistent outputs and higher latency on ~2% of requests; downstream QA flagged semantic drift causing failed assertions in their processing pipeline. Environment: prod-us-east, Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-2 (4x A100), orchestrator v1.8.3, edge-proxy v2.2.1. Observed window: 2026-03-08 18:12 - 18:46 UTC. Expected behavior: Explicitly pinned sessions should continue routing to the pinned model until pin expiry or explicit unpin. Workaround applied: Triggered manual pin-refresh job which reasserted lease tokens for affected tenant and restored routing for most sessions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy gptx-alpha-3.1 as a staged canary with 10% traffic for project atlassearch in prod-us-east
2) Simulate burst of NATed client reconnects to edge over 10-15 minutes (keepalive churn + retry)
3) Observe session-lease renewal rate at orchestrator and edge (look for >5x baseline jitter)
4) Watch routing table changes and per-tenant pin assignments in control plane over the window
logs: 2026-03-08T18:12:21Z edge-proxy[ingress] INFO tenant=atlassearch session=ks-9a3 lease-refresh=failed err=timeout
2026-03-08T18:12:23Z orchestrator[router] WARN tenant=atlassearch pin-check mismatch lease_ts_delta=+23s
2026-03-08T18:12:24Z serving-runtime[route] INFO routing-fallback tenant=atlassearch from=gptx-alpha-3.1 to=gptx-alpha-3.0-quant reason=pin-missing
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler/prewarm interaction caused rapid prewarm invalidation which cleared pin tombstones on edge shards.
Telemetry shows a correlated spike in session-lease-renew RPC errors from the edge to control plane coincident with CDN connection resets (us-east-1).
Control-plane snapshot/epoch showed a narrow window where pin lease timestamp differed between orchestrator replicas by ~20s (we log timestamps at millisecond granularity).
Edge probe logic treats missing/expired lease as eligible for fallback; combined with a commit-latency race the fallback path executed before lease reconciliation could recover.
Reproduced in a staging REPLAY: windowed reconnection pattern + induced RPC latency reproduces transient demotion in ~3/50 trials (non-deterministic).
impact_summary: Partial degraded routing for pinned sessions affecting AtlasSearch (dedicated). Approximately 2% of their traffic routed to quantized fallback, causing semantic divergence and a 60-120ms median latency increase for those requests.
customer_notes: AtlasSearch reported that their nightly QA jobs flagged content mismatches; they require a post-incident export of request IDs that hit fallbacks for compliance. Customer is on a dedicated plan and requested daily updates until fully resolved.
comments: Support (2026-03-08T19:05Z) - Priya: Acknowledged with AtlasSearch CSM. Running pin-refresh job as immediate mitigation. Requesting 2h window of elevated tracing for tenant.
SRE (2026-03-08T19:22Z) - Jordan Kim: Prelim logs show edge RPC timeouts coinciding with CDN edge churn. Raised a probe to capture edge->control plane RTTs for the tenant shard.

Eng (2026-03-08T20:10Z) - Marco: Confirmed orchestrator epoch skew: one replica applied snapshot 22s later under load. Short-term mitigation: make lease check resilient to 30s skew and defer fallback if pin seen recently.
Customer (AtlasSearch) (2026-03-08T21:00Z) - Sara M.: Thanks — please also provide the list of request IDs that saw fallback and approximate time window so we can reconcile QA failures.
root_cause: Race between edge lease-validation path and orchestrator snapshot application during a short window of high RPC latency; missing pin on edge shard led to fallback routing before control-plane reconciliation.
mitigation: Applied manual pin-refresh for AtlasSearch and toggled edge probe to extend grace window for lease staleness by +30s. Increased tracing retention for affected shard. Temporarily disabled aggressive fallback trigger while a patch is prepared.
next_steps: Patch: add conservative grace-period to edge fallback logic and tie to latest-orchestrator-epoch header (PR drafted: github.com/redwood-inference/orch/pull/4309)
Hardening: improve snapshot apply telemetry and add alert when replica snapshot-apply-latency > 10s
Postmortem: write a short postmortem and follow-up CL with QA replay harness to exercise reconnect patterns
Customer deliverable: export CSV of request IDs that hit fallback and scheduled 1:1 review with AtlasSearch engineer
resolution: Mitigation in progress; manual refresh restored >95% sessions. Patch underway and ETA for deploy to staging: 2026-03-11. Customer notified and CSM looped in.
